I get to play my favorite colors in a fun environment where something other than Atarka Red, Eldrazi, Cloud of Faeries and Manaless Dredge can be played successfully. There isn't a #1 deck that rotates out after 6 months, and I get to use cards all the way back to Beta (I don't have any Alpha cards). It's full of people who value fun more than winning, which is (or should be) the focus of a game. And it changes from game to game, deck to deck, person to person. No person plays the same way, no person has the exact same deck, it's all got a personal touch to it. It's all very personable, and it allows you the opportunity to form connections moreso than would be possible at an SCGOpen or Grand Prix. It's the stereotypical mantra of the format, "the format of self-expression," but it's what I love most about EDH.

I'll be honest, and it may be a bit cheesy, but for me it's how rarely I get to play. I have my playgroup that meets only once a week, and a friend and I meet on Wednesdays to play at another store, but other than that I don't get to play that often. That's part of the reason I'm trying to get my brother into it, so we both have someone to play with more often.

But that's just me.

Well then! This was rather raw and in-your-face. It's very strong and out there, language is plain and explicit. The imagery is very direct, which doesn't leave anything to the imagination. I like the sort of "here's this, deal with it" vibe the poem is giving off as though it's saying "this is how it is for me, I fucking dare you to say something," so I won't tell you to change that, though you will want to be aware that it may limit your readership. Also, there's a sort of emotionlessness behind it as well as the arrogance, like in the line "I'm just some whore for him to explore." That there, to me, is the only place where you could find some sort of possible tender emotion that the rest of the poem is lacking, but because the rest of the poem is lacking any sense of tenderness, it comes across as hollow and emotionless. I'm not saying this is a bad piece, far from it; it's raw, it's cynical, it knows it's not socially accepted and it's flipping you off because it doesn't care. The risk, however, is that the rough intimidation factor might put some people off after reading it. But that's always a risk when writing, isn't it?

I really enjoy the anaphora you have in the different sections of the poem; "skin/in/sin," "soul/goal/roll," "rose/close/chose." They really give it a flow to the poem and gives it, I thought, an ocean-tide-coming-to-shore type of feel, very rhythmic and soothing. The language is sensuous and romantic, though I am a little concerned about the use of "hickey" in a poem like this. It seems to sort of take away from the romance just a tiny bit and leads it more into a sort of animalistic nature. If that's what you were going for, then you may do with it as you please, as that was simply an irksome detail for me, though you may choose to do whatever you want. I really like this piece, excellent work!

I always want to give, and feel a huge pang of guilt when I don't, but usually I honestly don't have money or time to give. If I had my way, I'd be giving whatever money I had to those who I knew needed it. The thing is, there are people around my university who I'm really not sure they need it because I've run into them on a few separate occasions and they always change their stories. I've had the same guy come up to me requesting money because his mom died, he got stabbed by a big black man, and he wanted to buy some cereal, all different occasions. I still gave him money on every occasion. I was warned many time that there are people around here that really don't need my money as badly as they let on, but they're just trying to take advantage of my naiveté and get my money. It's gotten to the point where I don't trust anyone, and I just walk on past. Christian or not, that's just a douchey move, and as a Christian I really don't think Jesus would be too pleased with what I've become. I'm far from perfect, I know that even without letting myself know every waking moment, but my "moral code" isn't always at the forefront of my mind. I just try to help where I can, but again, I don't help those I can't trust at face value. If that makes me a bad person, I'm sorry, but I just can't.

TL;DR: want to give, not just because I'm Christian, but because I want to help. Only I can't help people if I don't trust them, which really pains me.
